messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT (P1) — KV-cache surge detected in us-west-2 / inference-pool. Continuous-batching avg batch size +1200% over baseline; KV cache miss rate spike -> tail latency > SLO. PagerDuty triggered.
Amber: acked. I'm on it — paging Priya and Samir. routing to on-call SREs.
Priya: on my way. any obvious customer  impact?
ops-bot: 5m window shows 504 proxy timeouts jump 0.3% -> 6.8%. Top affected routes: /v1/generate (sandbox, enterprise-xyz). Error traces point to slow kv lookups and very large batch formation.
Samir: confirm. KV hit rate dropped 0.78 -> 0.12. I think the batch-sizing tweak from this morning (`batch.size_factor=1.25`) is amplifying cold prefixes and filling batches with unique keys -> cache blowup.
Amber: can we roll that change back quickly? If we reduce batch factor we should reduce batch build-up and cache pressure.
Zach: I can push a hotfix to the runtime config. Proposing immediate rollback to `batch.size_factor=1.0` and disable `aggressive_kv_eviction` until warmup completes.
Priya: agree. Also seeing HPA oscillation on the pool: pods scale up when latency spikes then scale down quickly (scaleDown.stabilizationWindowSeconds low), which is making warmup worse. Need to lengthen stabilization and add prewarm annotation.
Samir: noted — the warmup path depends on a small set of cached keys being present in the KV shard. Rapid scale-down causes new pods to start cold and then get hammered.
Amber: timeline: 1) rollback batch config, 2) increase HPA scaleDown stabilization to 300s, 3) add prewarm annotation to new pods, 4) monitor latency and errors. Priya, are you able to apply the HPA patch? Zach, push the batch rollback?
Zach: pushing batch rollback now. command: 
```
# runtime config API (internal)
curl -X POST https://console.internal/api/configs/batching \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
  -d '{"batch_size_factor":1.0,"aggressive_kv_eviction":false}'
```
Zach: rollback submitted, response 202. Applying to us-west-2 primary serving pool first.
Priya: patching HPA behavior. running: 
```
kubectl patch hpa inference-pool-hpa -n inference --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/behavior/scaleDown/stabilizationWindowSeconds","value":300}]'
```
Priya: done. also adding `redwood.com/prewarm=true` pod annotation on the deployment to trigger kv warmup sidecar.
Samir: I'm also toggling `kv.prefetch_threshold=0.6` lower to be conservative during warmup. doing via rollout to canary subset first.
Amber: good. putting a temporary rate-limit on sandbox customers to reduce burst while we stabilize: `quota.sandbox=0.5qps`. Ops, please confirm.
Zach: applied sandbox throttle via rate-limit service.
ops-bot: Metric updates: 10m after rollback — avg batch size trending down  +1200% -> +120% (still high), KV hit rate improving 0.12 -> 0.46, 504s down from 6.8% -> 1.9%.
Priya: HPA oscillation reduced. new stabilization window seems to stop the immediate scale-down. Prewarm annotations showing initial KV fetches on new pods.
Samir: watching tail latency — p95 improved but p99 still elevated. likely need a few more warmup cycles.
Amber: I'm going to hand this to Priya for the evening rotation. I'll remain reachable for escalation. Priya, estimated time to steady state?
Priya: taking over. estimate 45-60m to return to baseline p99 once cache warmup finishes across shards. I'll keep one of the SREs watching dashboards and spike alerts.
Amber: thanks — handing off. I'll record notes in the incident channel and start an incident doc template.
Priya: ack. I'll also create a short postmortem draft and include: cause hypotheses (batch.size_factor change + inadequate HPA stabilization), mitigation steps (rollback, throttling, HPA config, prewarm), and follow-ups (load-testing for new batch configs, automated warmup, alert tuning).
ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: 40m after mitigation — p99 within 10% of baseline, KV hit-rate 0.72, error rate 504s 0.6%. No customer escalations received in the last 30m.
Samir: rolling back the canary of `kv.prefetch_threshold` to conservative default once stable.
Priya: closing the active page, will convert to follow-up task. Please add any notes you saw in thread to the incident doc.
ops-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — page closed. Please file postmortem and include timeline + config diffs.
Amber: thanks team — good catch and quick rollback. Follow-up items: automated canary tests for batch changes, HPA stability guard rails, and a playbook entry for cache blowups.
Priya: will own postmortem.
Zach: capturing the commands I ran in the incident doc.
Samir: will add monitoring dashboards for kv-prefetch and batch-size distributions.
Amber: handing final ack. :thumbsup:
